[[Hanover Park F.C.|Hanover Park]] | matches = 170 | total goals = 431 | average goals = | league topscorer = | biggest home win = | biggest away win = | highest scoring = | longest wins = | longest unbeaten = | longest winless = | longest losses = | highest attendance = | lowest attendance = | average attendance = | prevseason = [[2009–10 National First Division|2009–10]] | nextseason = [[2011–12 National First Division|2011–12]] }} '''2010–11 National First Division''', was the season from September 2010 until May 2011, of South Africa's second tier of professional [[association football|football]]. The overall NFD champion was promoted to the first level, known as [[Premier Soccer League]] (PSL). While the losing team of the championship final, faced a round robin playoff stage, against the second lowest ranked team of PSL and the two second ranked teams of the NFD streams. ==Season structure== The league is made up of 16 teams, split into 2 streams. Each team plays the other 7 teams in their stream 3 times, for a total of 21 games. Teams receive 3 points for a win, 1 for draw, and 0 for a loss. At the end of the season, the top ranked team from each stream play in a two-legged final, the winner of which is crowned National First Division Champion, and gains automatic promotion to the Premier Soccer League for the next season. The loser of the final, along with the teams which came second in their streams, and the 15th placed PSL team, go into the PSL promotion play-offs. The two teams finishing in last place in their streams are automatically relegated to the Vodacom League. They are replaced by the finalists of the [[Vodacom]] League championship game.{{citation needed|date=September 2017}} ==Club and stadium information== '''Coastal Stream (excl. The log therefore ended to award the second place for Black Leopards.{{cite web|url=http://www.kickoff.com/news/21804/black-leopards-look-set-for-psl-promotional-playoffs.php|title=Black Leopards look set for PSL promotional playoffs -Leopards win appeal against PSL ruling |author=KickOff|date=2011-05-17}} |col_C=green1|text_C=[[National First Division|NFD]] Inland Stream Champions 2010/2011 |result1=C |col_QP=yellow1|text_QP=Qualification for PSL promotion play-offs |result2=QP |col_R=red1|text_R=Relegation to the [[Vodacom League]] |result8=R |update=complete|source= }} ===Postseason=== ====NFD Final==== The winner of the two streams, [[Bay United F.C.|Bay United]] and [[Jomo Cosmos]] will meet and play a two legged tie, on 14 May and 22 May, to determine the overall 2010–11 NFD championship. The NFD champion will gain an automatic promotion to the [[Premier Soccer League|PSL]]. While the looser of the NFD Final will get a second chance to promote to PSL, at the Promotion Play Offs. {{TwoLeg start}} {{TwoLegResult|[[Bay United F.C.|Bay United]]|ZAF| 0–0

[http://www.psl.co.za/article.asp%3Fid%3D418438 report]}} {{end}} ====Promotion playoffs==== The losing team of the NFD Final ([[Bay United F.C.|Bay United]]), together with both runner-ups of the NFD streams ([[Thanda Royal Zulu FC|Thanda Royal Zulu]] and [[Black Leopards F.C.|Black Leopards]]), and finally the second lowest ranked team of PSL ([[Vasco da Gama (South Africa)|Vasco da Gama]]), entered into the promotion playoffs. This playoff competition was played as a cup with two legged matches, with an unseeded draw to decide the fixtures.{{cite web|url=http://www.kickoff.com/news/21643/first-division-promotional-play-off-draw-held.php|title=NFD Play-off draw completed|author=KickOff|date=2011-05-09}} The two semifinals were scheduled to be played simultaneously at 25 and 29 May. Due to Black Leopards having qualified for the [[2011 Nedbank Cup]] final at 28 May, the two semifinals were however rescheduled, to be played at 8 and 11 June. A two legged final with the two winning teams from the semifinal, was played on 15 and 18 June.{{cite web|url=http://www.psl.co.za/article.asp?id=418141|title=Leopards change play-off fixture|author=PSL|date=2011-05-20|access-date=2011-05-22|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120314015859/http://www.psl.co.za/article.asp?id=418141|archive-date=2012-03-14|url-status=dead}} Only the winner of the promotion playoff final was get promoted to play the next season in PSL.{{fact|date=July 2023}} '''Semifinals:''' {{TwoLeg start}} {{TwoLegResult|'''[[Bay United F.C.|Bay United]]'''|ZAF | 4–1 | [[Thanda Royal Zulu FC|Thanda Royal Zulu]]|ZAF |0–0
